title: My favorite part of every telecast is seeing what all the shows choos...
transcript: Here is what I would have every show perform if I was in charge of the Tony Awards. starting with new musicals, For Lost Boys, I would do a medley. Start with “belong to someone” and showcase the flying, if they're able to do that. Then go into “wild” to show off Shoshana Bean, their Tony nominee, and then end with “have to have you,” which is just a bop. for two strangers, I'd go with “New York.” I know they've done that song a lot, but it really does perfectly capture the vibes of the show. It perfectly showcases the dynamic between Robin and Dougal. And they can do the duet version that they've been doing on talk shows that showcases Christiani a little bit more. For Titanique, obviously, you have to do “My Heart Will Go on.” But I think I would start with “I'm alive” just to introduce the concept of the show, and then end with a “my heart will go on” Sing-along. for Schmigadoon, I think you have to do “corn puddin.” In this one song, you immediately understand the concept of the show. It is a town where people randomly break out into song. Melissa's very into it. Josh is not. Plus, you get to show off that amazing Chris Gattelli choreography. Before we get to the revivals, I wanna touch on some of the special performances we're getting. We know that we're getting a book of Mormon 15th anniversary performance. They Kind of have to do a medley in order to show off the entire company. So I'd probably do something like “hello” into “all American prophet,” into “Sal Tlay Ka Siti”, into “tomorrow is a latter day.” But even that feels really light on Josh Gad and Rory O'malley, So I don't know. This is a hard one. We have Rachel Zegler doing a performance from a Chorus Line. The obvious answer here is “what I did for love,” although I would love to hear her version of “nothing” as well. Leslie Odom Jr is singing a song from rent for the in Memoriam. I feel like “without you” makes the most sense, But an “I'll cover you Reprise” would wreck me. Okay, finally, the revivals. I think you start with “Time Warp” and then go into “Sweet T” The songs flow into each other nicely, and it highlights both their most iconic song and the performer in the show that everyone is talking about. For cats the Jellicle ball, I feel like you have to do Jellicle songs for Jellicle cats. And then finally, for ragtime, I feel like you have to do the prologue.
